'''E-3PO''', mockingly referred to as '''E-Gregious''' by Imperial support teams, was an [[E-3PO]] [[Protocol droid/Legends|protocol droid]] in the service of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]]. Known for his gruff manners and vulgar demeanor, E-3PO's true allegiances lied with [[IG-88's Droid Army]], a [[droid supremacy]] collective that had infiltrated [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]]. Following the [[Battle of Hoth/Legends|Battle of Hoth]], the protocol droid acted as a liason between Imperial and [[Ugnaught/Legends|Ugnaught]] technicians on [[Cloud City/Legends|Cloud City]] during the Empire's hunt for the [[Millennium Falcon/Legends|''Millennium Falcon'']].

==Biography==
{{Quote|Boba Fett has gone to the garbage recycling level. Han Solo has not yet arrived, although moments ago our perimeter scanners reported a ship matching the description of the ''Millennium Falcon'' entering the system. It appears to have some hyperdrive damage.|E-3PO to IG-88B|<ref name="IG-88" />}}
E-3PO was constructed on the manufacturing [[Planet/Legends|world]] [[Mechis III/Legends|Mechis III]] during the [[Imperial Era/Legends|Imperial Era]]. Unbeknownst to the organic population of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]], the planet had been [[Mechis III Uprising|taken over]] by a quartet of rogue [[IG-88 assassin droid/Legends|IG-88 assassin droids]] that utilized Mechis III's [[Droid/Legends|droid]] factories to produce an [[IG-88's Droid Army|army]]. Programmed with upgraded [[Sentience/Legends|sentience]], these droids, E-CPO among them, were sent off into the galaxy and told to operate as expected until the time was right to begin the [[Droid Revolution]].<ref name="IG-88" />

Attached to [[Death Squadron/Legends|Death Squadron]], E-3PO was transported to [[Cloud City/Legends|Cloud City]] in [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]] to serve as translator liaison with the colony's [[Ugnaught/Legends|Ugnaught]] engineers during the hunt for [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]].<ref name="CCG">{{CCG|set=Cloud City Limited|cardname=E-3PO}}</ref> When [[IG-88B/Legends|IG-88B]] arrived on [[Bespin/Legends|Bespin]] to capture [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] and stop [[Boba Fett/Legends|Boba Fett]] from getting the [[Bounty/Legends|bounty]] on the [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggler]], E-3PO acted as his informant, supplying the [[Assassin droid/Legends|assassin droid]] with a detailed map of the facility before continuing about his regular business.<ref name="IG-88" />

[[File:E-3POandC-3PO.jpg|thumb|left|250px|C-3PO and E-3PO.]]
Unhappy with his situation on Bespin, E-3PO believed the Empire was bent on destroying him by forcing him to work with a culture specialized in the disassembly and reprocessing of salvageable [[Droid/Legends|droids]] and droid parts. The Imperial team helping the Ugnaughts convert the [[Carbon-freezing/Legends|carbon freezing]] chamber's chemical intermix ratio for [[Human/Legends|Human]] hibernation took to calling E-3PO "E-Gregious" because of his outlandish attitude. Insulted, he left the chamber,<ref name="db" /> taking time only to mumble "[[E chu ta/Legends|E chu ta]]!" to [[C-3PO/Legends|C-3PO]] standing outside the door, who commented on his rudeness.<ref name="Episode V" />

==Characteristics==
E-3PO was known to be arrogant, rude, and vulgar.<ref name="CCG" /> However, when faced with any pushback to his attitude, the droid would become offended.<ref name="db" /> IG-88B attributed E-3PO's brusque behavior to the successful sentience programming the protocol droid had undergone on Mechis III, though the assassin droid worried that his spy was perhaps too uncouth, to the point of potentially arousing suspicion among organics.<ref name="IG-88" />

==Behind the scenes==
E-3PO was portrayed by [[Chris Parsons]] in [[Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back|''Star Wars'': Episode V ''The Empire Strikes Back'']], who also portrayed [[4-LOM/Legends|4-LOM]] and [[K-3PO/Legends|K-3PO]] in the same film.
